subject: Contract runway & surge plan: MediaScout renewal prep
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jack Reilly <jack.reilly@mediascout.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Contract runway & surge plan: MediaScout renewal prep

Hi Jack —

Quick note ahead of our renewal window: I pulled together a short usage runway and three commercial options that can help cover your seasonal campaign spikes without surprising overage invoices. Key observations from the last 90 days (attached):

- 45% month-over-month spike during the June campaign (peaks to 6x baseline for 48 hours)
- Average latency within our hosted API SLO (p50 ~18ms, p95 ~120ms) but you reported a handful of 95th percentile timeouts during peak bursts
- Prefix caching reduced repeat token spend on templated prompts by ~12% for authorship flows

Attachments: [Attachment: Q3_usage_report.csv (csv)] [Attachment: elastic-pricing-illustration.xlsx (xlsx)]

High-level options (short):
1) Short-term elastic uplift (no term): pay-as-you-go with a burst buffer + 30% uplift credit for first 30 days to smooth spikes
2) 12-month committed token package: lower per-token rate + rollover credits; recommended if you expect sustained higher baseline after marketing ramps
3) Dedicated pool pilot: for sustained high throughput and lower p95 latency — includes a 30-day trial period and migration assistance

Can we do 30 minutes this week to walk numbers with Marissa (CS) and Lauren (billing)? If you share your preferred time I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

From: Jack Reilly <jack.reilly@mediascout.com>

Cc: support@mediascout.com
Date: 2027-08-09T11:15:12-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract runway & surge plan: MediaScout renewal prep

Aditya —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. A few quick points from our side:

- The June spike was campaign-driven and will likely repeat in October; we need assurance the burst doesn't blow the budget.
- A handful of our product engineers saw timeouts during campaign peaks; before we commit to a 12-month package we need clarity on p95 improvements (we're targeting sub-100ms).
- Can you give an apples-to-apples cost comparison (net of credits) for the next 6 months if we pick Elastic vs Commit? Also, what flexibility do you offer if our projected 6-month usage drops below the committed minimum?

Happy to meet — mornings PST are best on Thursday/Friday.

—Jack
Head of Platform, MediaScout
jack.reilly@mediascout.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jack Reilly <jack.reilly@mediascout.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract runway & surge plan: MediaScout renewal prep

Jack —

Thanks for the quick reply. Looping in Marissa (CS) and Lauren (billing) to join the call and help run the scenario math. High-level apples-to-apples for the next 6 months (ballpark, shown net of introductory credits):

- Elastic (pay-as-you-go + burst buffer): estimated spend $62k — good for irregular spikes, no long-term commitment, higher peak unit cost
- 6-month committed (prorated from 12-month pricing): estimated spend $49k — lower unit cost, includes 10% rollover credit and one-time migration assistance if you adopt dedicated routing
- Dedicated pilot (30 days): setup + pilot ~$15k one-time + variable after pilot depending on pool sizing

Flexibility: for committed packages we offer a built-in downward adjustment window at the 3-month mark (up to one tier down) and limited token rollover. For shortfalls beyond the committed minimum we provide a 2-month grace buffer before standard true-up charges; for long-term shortfalls we can discuss buy-down options tied to timing of the shortfall.

Attached: [Attachment: SLA_draft-v2.pdf (pdf)] — this includes the p95/p99 targets and our escalation path. On p95: with the recommended Dedicated pilot we typically see p95 drop under 95ms for workloads like yours because of reserved GPU capacity and reduced multi-tenant interference. If you prefer to stay on hosted, Marissa can propose configuration/quant profiles to tighten the p95 without immediate migration.

Proposed next steps:
- 30-min sync with Marissa & Lauren this Thursday at 9:30 AM PST (I can send invite)
- If you want, we can model two 6-month spend scenarios with your October campaign included and attach a one-page summary for procurement

Let me know if Thursday 9:30 works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Aditya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Contract runway & surge plan: MediaScout renewal prep

Aditya / Lauren / Vivek —

Notes from CS perspective before we speak with Jack:

- Recommendation: lead with the 6-month committed pricing (prorated 12mo) + a 30-day "surge protection" credit equal to 10% of committed tokens applied during the first two heavy campaigns. This gives MediaScout budget predictability and protection for immediate spikes.
- If they insist on no term, offer Elastic with a 30-day introductory 25% burst buffer at our standard pay-as-you-go rate but include a one-time discount of 5% on the first invoice to offset early campaign variance.
- For the p95/timeouts: CS will run a short test harness against a representative job (we need a sample payload). That test can be completed in 48 hours and will provide a p95 comparison hosted vs dedicated.

Negotiation levers to keep in pocket: 10% first-month credit (exec approval), extended payment terms (net-60) if they commit to 12-month minimum, limited professional services hours for migration included in the committed package.

If we go with the 6-month commit proposal I suggest we request a non-binding letter of intent after the call so procurement can start internal approvals.

—Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Proposal & next steps: MediaScout contract package

Jack —

Thanks again for the quick responses yesterday. Based on our internal discussion (summary below) we recommend the 6-month committed package as the middle ground between predictability and flexibility. Below is the explicit offer and next steps.

Recommended offer (summary):
- 6-month committed token package (prorated from 12mo pricing) — estimated spend $49,000 over 6 months
- Surge protection: 10% token credit for the first two campaign periods (applied automatically)
- p95 assistance: CS will run a 48-hour test harness against one representative job to validate p95 improvements; dedicated pilot only if the test shows >20% latency improvement
- Billing flex: net-60 payment terms available with signed LOI

Attachments: [Attachment: Q3_usage_report.csv (csv)] [Attachment: SLA_draft-v2.pdf (pdf)] [Attachment: elastic-pricing-illustration.xlsx (xlsx)]

If that aligns, next steps:
1) Quick 30-min call to confirm LOI language and finalize committed token quantity — Thursday 9:30 AM PST (I’ll send a calendar invite)
2) We’ll run the 48-hour latency test (Marissa will need a sample payload)
3) Lauren will prepare a one-page SOW/price sheet and DocuSign link for the LOI

Calendar: https://calendly.com/aditya-redwood/30min
DocuSign LOI (preview): https://docusign.com/rdw-prop/8347
